page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6.6xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8269CY processor utilizing x86_64 architecture, offering 24 dedicated virtual CPU cores. The instance features 96.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per virtual core. It does not include integrated hardware accelerators or GPUs, nor does it bundle any local ephemeral storage disks, requiring all persistent storage volumes to be attached through cloud network storage.

Network connectivity on the instance provides a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps. Because it operates with dedicated vCPUs rather than shared or burstable compute allocations, execution performance remains stable across continuous CPU-intensive processing tasks. Architectural tradeoffs center on the lack of built-in local NVMe storage and complementary public IPv4 addresses, which necessitates planning for remote block storage and virtual networking configurations.

From an efficiency standpoint, the balanced compute-to-memory ratio provides a standard hardware profile suitable for mid-to-large multi-threaded enterprise services. Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6.6xlarge is aligned with workloads such as enterprise web serving, backend application servers, container clusters, relational database hosting, continuous integration pipelines, and general distributed systems that require dependable memory capacity per thread.

It is suited for enterprise application backends, containerized workloads, distributed services, databases, and moderate-to-heavy web serving infrastructure.
